deckTitle: MedKayfab: Mnemetic Medicine Mayhem — Anti-Rule Book
verdict: The Anti-Rule Book is the missing piece every MedKayfab table needs. Fifteen comic spreads replace a 40-page PDF manual without a single yawn. Strongest asset: 'Calls from the Ringside' (BINGO/BONGO/BOGGLE/BLÖDSINN) hands players a living table vocabulary before they've touched a card. The Quest Die Arc (p.11) is the only page that risks cognitive overload on first read — dense but recoverable. Table-ready: YES.
blurb: The only rulebook that burns its own genre to the ground. One comic, 15 spreads, and you're running your first clinical story wrestling match in under two minutes.

coverQA.coverVisual: 5 — FrizzleBob torching medical textbooks surrounded by lucha libre pathogens. Full-bleed, explosive, immediately signals anarchy + medicine.
coverQA.coverTitle: 5 — 'Mnemetic Medicine Mayhem' is alliterative gold. Subtitle ('Anti-Rule Book for the Clinical Story Wrestling Game') delivers the elevator pitch in one breath.
coverQA.coverVibeMatch: 5 — Cover IS the game: chaotic, educational, absurdist. Perfect alignment with everything inside.
coverQA.coverOriginality: 5 — Nothing else in medical education looks like this. Zero confusion with competitors.
coverQA.coverViral: 5 — Burning medical textbooks is a provocation that stops thumbs mid-scroll. Share-bait for medstudent Twitter.
coverQA.coverNote: Possibly the strongest cover in the MedKayfab corpus. The 'REDACTED' hospital documents flanking FrizzleBob do double duty: they signal satire AND reference the Corporate Hospital antagonist the rules introduce on page 2. Nothing is wasted.

notes: Pure rules document, no card grid pages. 15 pages: 1 cover + 14 themed spreads each teaching one mechanic. Structure is exemplary: pitch (p.2) → components (p.3) → quick start (p.4) → intro ritual (p.5) → stage mechanics (p.6) → turn steps (p.7) → die faces 1-3 (p.8) + 4-6 (p.9) → performance philosophy (p.10) → quest arc (p.11) → table vocab (p.12) → finale+log (p.13) → solo play (p.14) → cheat sheet (p.15). Each spread uses character examples (Badger/Fox/Owl/Bear) to show not tell. 'Stay fluffy!' appears organically as a recurring micro-brand. BLÖDSINN embedded in English text is deliberate cultural collision. No RAF boxes, no card slots.

quickWins: Add 'Common Mistakes' or FAQ micro-panel to the Quick Start spread
Consider a one-page visual index mapping deck types to Quest Die stages
niceToHave: Versioned update mechanism as gameplay evolves
QR code on cheat sheet linking to digital Mechanism Log template
